title: Engine and settings
description: What the engine can do, its settings (kept across documents), and the frame announcement.

engine.hello.summary: Tells the engine which protocol the client speaks; a client calls it first. The engine answers with the protocol it will speak (this version: 1) or refuses one it does not know (unsupported), so that when the protocol changes, old and new clients can be told apart.

engine.info.summary: The engine's version, the grids and solvers it knows, the machine's threads, and its methods.

protocol.description: Raised when a change breaks clients.

supported.description: This version solves its puzzles: every grid (stacking since the deferred plan's part 3b).

defaultSize.description: The size of a new shape in each direction, in cells.

sizeUnit.description: shape.resize counts in blocks of this many cells.

convertsTo.description: The grids document.convertGrid converts its puzzles to (the original's Convert brick grid type to other): rhombic and tetraOcta for bricks, none for the others.

slidingSolvers.description: The solver of sliding puzzles, one: the Sliding Puzzle Solver (the Solver Type a sliding puzzle shows; there is none to choose).

stackingSolvers.description: The solvers of stacking puzzles (SolveOptions.stacking.solver), with the original's menu labels. The original offered one, by the problem's rod set: the Panex Solver for Panex columns, else the Stacking Solver, which a solve without a solver named uses too.

memoryBytes.description: The machine's physical memory in bytes; 0 when it cannot be read. The automatic searchMemoryGB is half of it.

engine.shutdown.summary: Replies, then ends the engine: its solves pause and are waited for (end of input does the same).

settings.set.summary: Changes some settings; the others stay. A smaller undo depth drops the oldest steps.

frame.summary: Announces a binary frame: exactly 'bytes' raw bytes follow this line at once; the reply that refers to it comes after.

threads.description: The threads of a solve when its options do not say; 0 every hardware thread (default).

solver.description: The solver when a solve's or analysis's options do not say (default classic).

slideFolder.description: Where a sliding search keeps its older levels while it runs, in a folder of its own that goes when it ends (the original's SHAPELOGIC_SLIDE_DIR); empty keeps them in memory. Default: the user's cache folder's sliding folder.

slideDiskGB.description: The disk those levels may take, in GB (SHAPELOGIC_SLIDE_DISK_GB); 0, the default: half the free space, at most 200 GB. More than the disk has room for is held to its free space but a reserve (2 GB or a twentieth of it). On macOS the free space counts what the system frees on demand, as Finder does.

panexFolder.description: Where a stacking solve's Panex search saves itself, in a folder per puzzle (the original's SHAPELOGIC_PANEX_DIR): a paused stacking solve is its saved search there, which solve.continue carries on (also after the engine or the document ended), solve.start and solve.abort throw away, solve.status describes, and the paused solve's export and import carry. Empty saves nothing (a search that outgrows its memory then finds its path by solving halves again). Default: the user's cache folder's panex folder.

panexDiskGB.description: The disk a saved search's levels may take, in GB (SHAPELOGIC_PANEX_DISK_GB); 0, the default: half the free space, at most 200 GB. The fuller it gets, the fewer levels are kept and the longer finding the path at the end takes. More than the disk has room for is held to its free space but a reserve, as slideDiskGB is.

searchMemoryGB.description: The memory a sliding or stacking search may fill, in GB; 0, the default: half the machine's memory (engine.info's memoryBytes), at least 2 GB. It decides every solve's memory: a solve's highMemory plays no part, and a note of a search that ran out of memory or disk names Settings ▸ Solver.
